newsitem.title: UK: UK CBI's Barker favours independent BOE.
newsitem.headline: UK CBI's Barker favours independent BOE.

text.p: Kate Barker, economic adviser to the Confederation of British Industry (CBI) and a member of the Treasury's panel of independent economic advisers, said she would welcome more independence for the Bank of England.

"Certainly from a business standpoint, we would welcome any move that makes the Bank of England more independent," she told BBC Radio Four. "We also, of course, welcome any move that makes the Bank...draw on a wide range of opinion."
"In the longer run we would prefer to see the Bank independent in day to day and month to month decisions, taking those decisions right out of the political arena."
Barker was commenting on proposals by the opposition Labour party to change the institutional arrangements for framing monetary policy.
She said it was not clear from remarks by Labour finance spokesman Gordon Brown whether his proposed Council of Economic Advisers would be full-time or part-time.
"I think one of the strengths of the present panel has been that we have all got full-time jobs elsewhere and brought the experience of those jobs into the Treasury," Barker said.
Independence had been a great strength as it meant panel members had "no financial allegiance" to the government.
Barker said Brown had not made it clear when and if he would move towards an independent central bank.

"If we were going to go into European monetary union, then an independent central bank has to be clearly established really well in advance. It would help towards that, but it's not a clear step in that direction."
"I think it still has a strong element of wait-and-see," she added.
